title: Grades 3–5 Mini Test — Reading: The Recycling Project
overview: A short reading practice. Read about a class recycling project. Use the passage, the chart, and the table to answer six questions.

sections.title: The Room 12 Recycling Project
sections.directions: Read the passage. Then answer the questions. You can look back at the passage, the chart, and the table as many times as you want.

items.title: Why They Started
items.prompt: Why did Room 12 start a recycling project?
passage: At Harbor View Elementary, the students in Room 12 wanted to make less trash. Their teacher, Mr. Mensah, helped them start a recycling project.

First, the class learned which things can be recycled. Paper, cardboard, plastic bottles, and metal cans can be made into new things. Food scraps cannot go in the recycling bin, but they can go in a compost bin to make rich soil for plants.
Next, the class put three bins in the lunchroom: a blue bin for recycling, a green bin for compost, and a gray bin for trash. Students made signs with pictures so everyone knew where to put things.
Every Friday, the class weighed the recycling. After four weeks, they were proud of what they found. The school was recycling more and throwing away less trash every week!
items.correct: Correct. The students wanted to make less trash.
items.hint: Read the first sentence of the passage.
